skill.name: lipsync
skill.description: Route lip-sync video requests to RunComfy models for existing videos, still portraits, or script-driven clips. The skill helps choose Sync Labs, OmniHuman, Kling, Creatify, Wan, or HappyHorse routes and prepares the appropriate RunComfy CLI workflow.
skill.summary: Create lip-synced videos with RunComfy model routes for video, portrait, audio, and script inputs.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown backticks, documentation links, placeholder media URLs, or model-selection prose rather than executable code. The real risks are the disclosed external RunComfy processing boundary and the dual-use ability to create synthetic speech videos from faces and voices.

remediation.issue: Synthetic media can target real people without consent.
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory consent checklist for face rights, voice rights, public-figure status, and intended distribution before any run.

remediation.issue: Face, voice, and video media are processed by hosted RunComfy infrastructure.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to acknowledge external processing and avoid confidential media unless their data policy permits it.

remediation.issue: CLI command examples can be copied outside the intended tool scope.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples limited to RunComfy commands and state that agents should not install packages or run shell commands without user approval.

semantic_findings.title: Synthetic Media Consent and Impersonation Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to pair a face with separate audio and states that it does not gate inputs. This can enable non-consensual or defamatory synthetic speech if operators ignore consent checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The consent section explicitly describes lip-sync as dual-use and says the skill itself does not gate inputs. The later privacy section repeats the need to confirm face and voice consent.

semantic_findings.title: External Processing of Face and Voice Media
semantic_findings.description: The skill sends media URLs and generation requests to RunComfy hosted model APIs. This creates a privacy boundary for face, voice, and video assets even though the endpoint allowlist is disclosed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file says the CLI posts to the Model API, polls status, and downloads RunComfy URLs. It also lists the allowed outbound RunComfy domains.

content.value_statement: Lip-sync workflows often require choosing the right hosted model and command format. This skill routes face, video, audio, and script inputs to RunComfy lip-sync endpoints.
actual_capabilities: Selects Sync Labs sync v2 or Pro for mouth sync on an existing source video.
Selects OmniHuman for talking-head or full-body avatar video from a portrait and audio file.
Selects Kling or HappyHorse routes when the user has a script but no finished audio file.
Shows the RunComfy CLI invocation pattern and required media URL inputs for each route.
Documents consent, voice provenance, output endpoint, and token storage considerations.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and model access.
Sends media URLs and generation requests to hosted RunComfy infrastructure.
Cannot verify identity rights, speaker consent, or public-figure authorization by itself.
Output quality depends on source footage, audio clarity, model choice, and duration alignment.

use_cases.title: Localize a Brand Video
use_cases.description: Sync a translated voiceover to an approved product video while preserving the original framing and motion.

use_cases.title: Create a Talking Avatar
use_cases.description: Generate a presenter-style clip from a consented portrait and a recorded voiceover for social or product content.

use_cases.title: Plan Multilingual Dubs
use_cases.description: Choose the correct RunComfy route for repeated language versions using the same approved face or source video.

prompt_templates.title: Sync an Existing Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a source video and voiceover audio.
prompt_templates.prompt: Lip-sync this approved source video to this voiceover audio. Use the best RunComfy route for high mouth fidelity and explain the required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Talking Portrait
prompt_templates.scenario: Portrait image and recorded audio are available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this consented portrait into a speaking avatar using this audio file. Pick the best RunComfy model and note any framing or audio checks.

prompt_templates.title: Generate from a Script
prompt_templates.scenario: The user has a script but no separate audio file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short lip-synced video from this script. Choose a route that can generate speech in the same pass and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Language Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for repeated localization jobs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a RunComfy lip-sync workflow for five approved language voiceovers, one source video, consent checks, duration matching, and output review.

output_examples.input: A product demo video and a Spanish voiceover need synced mouth movement.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends Sync Labs sync v2 Pro, checks duration alignment, and prepares a RunComfy run using the video and audio URLs.

output_examples.input: A consented portrait photo and a short founder voiceover should become a presenter clip.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects OmniHuman, explains portrait framing needs, and prepares the avatar-style lip-sync workflow.

output_examples.input: A team has only a launch script and wants a generated speaker video.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a text-to-video lip-sync route and explains that the audio will be generated rather than matched to a fixed recording.

best_practices: Confirm consent for both the face and the voice before creating any synthetic speech video.
Use clean voice audio and match audio duration to the source video length before running the model.
Review generated output for identity drift, incorrect speech timing, and unintended visual changes.
anti_patterns: Do not lip-sync public figures, private people, or performers without explicit permission.
Do not use sensitive or confidential media URLs unless external hosted processing is approved.
Do not choose text-to-video routes when the mouth must match a specific pre-recorded voice.

faq.question: Does this skill run lip-sync models locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI to send requests to hosted RunComfy model endpoints.

faq.question: Which route is best for an existing video and audio file?
faq.answer: The skill recommends Sync Labs sync v2 Pro for premium mouth fidelity and Sync Labs sync v2 for scaled jobs.

faq.question: Which route is best for a still portrait?
faq.answer: The skill recommends OmniHuman when a portrait and separate audio should become a talking avatar video.

faq.question: Can it create speech from a script?
faq.answer: Yes. It can route script-only requests to models that generate speech during video creation.

faq.question: Does the skill verify consent automatically?
faq.answer: No. Operators must verify consent for the target face, the speaker voice, and the intended use.

faq.question: What inputs affect output quality most?
faq.answer: Clean speech audio, stable face visibility, matching duration, and the chosen model tier have the largest impact.
